en.text: The rotation of cotton in the kharif season followed by wheat in the rabi season, and then mungbean (green gram) in the next kharif, is a good fit for your farm because it balances water use and soil health. Cotton needs a lot of water – about 723 mm more than it gets – so the rotation includes mungbean, a nitrogen‑fixing legume, to build soil nitrogen for the next wheat crop. The soil health score of 69 and the soil suitability score of 73 show that the soil can support this mix. Climate data show that the recent kharif rainfall has risen by about 90 mm and the maximum temperature has dropped by 0.8 °C, which is a positive trend for your area. Watch out for the high water deficit in cotton and the 52 hot days that can stress the crop; you may need extra irrigation. 1. Plant mungbean after cotton to add nitrogen to the soil – this reduces the need for fertilizer next year. 2. Keep residue from cotton on the field to improve soil moisture and structure. 3. Use a local extension officer to confirm the irrigation plan and crop timing before you start planting.
en.technical_note: The rotation score shows a water_fit of 28 and a soil_health of 69, indicating moderate water stress but good soil structure. Cotton’s water deficit of 723 mm and 52 heat stress days highlight the need for supplemental irrigation. Mungbean’s nitrogen fixation (KB: Agronomic guidance on legume nitrogen fixation) will reduce the nitrogen requirement for the following wheat crop. Climate shift data (NASA POWER) show a 90 mm increase in kharif rainfall and a 0.8 °C drop in mean maximum temperature, improving water availability and reducing heat stress.

en.question: Why was this rotation recommended for my farm?

response.answer: The rotation was chosen because it balances water use, heat risk, and soil health for your farm. Cotton in the kharif season has a water deficit of 723 mm, so the rotation includes a nitrogen‑fixing legume (mungbean) in the next kharif to build soil nitrogen and reduce the need for extra fertilizer. The rotation also improves soil health (score 68) and takes advantage of the recent increase in kharif rainfall to 402 mm, which helps meet cotton’s water demand. Finally, the heat risk score is moderate (50) and the critical temperature for cotton is 38 °C, so the rotation keeps hot days within tolerable limits.
